did_you_know.text: The tribes in the northern part of the land are allotted horizontal strips extending from the eastern border to the sea. From north to south, the order is Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah.
Between Judah’s inheritance and the central area, a sacred allotment is set aside, 25,000 wide and extending from east to west; the temple is located within it.
The sacred allotment for the priests is a rectangle 25,000 long and 10,000 wide, with the LORD’s sanctuary at its center.
The priests appointed to serve in the sacred area are the descendants of Zadok, who are described as having kept their duty to the LORD and not gone astray when others did.
Alongside the priests’ allotment, an inheritance is assigned to the Levites, measuring 25,000 long and 10,000 wide.
The priests’ sacred lands may not be sold, exchanged, or transferred, because they are designated as holy to the LORD.
The remaining area of the allotment is designated for the city, housing, and open land. The city lies within this area, which is not considered sacred.
The city measures 4,500 on each of its four sides, so it is described as a square-shaped city.
The land remaining to the east and west of the sacred allotment and the city’s property is assigned to the prince, with the central area lying between the inheritances of Judah and Benjamin.
The city has three gates on each side, and its name summarizes its central purpose: “The LORD Is There.” Its circumference is 18,000.
